title: allocation-visibility-statement-aug-2027
content:
Purpose:
This operator-facing snapshot provides a compact per-contract allocation and utilization view for the Dedicated GPU fleet (hosted pools) so on-call and infra planners can make fast decisions about temporary slices, soft evictions, or migration windows. Not a final ledger; complements the contract ledger and reservation trackers.

Summary: 
- Fleet covered: us-west1, us-east4, eu-west1, ap-southeast1 (A100s-v4 and A10G mixed pools).
- Window: rolling 30-day utilization (2027-07-16 to 2027-08-15) with runway forecast to 2027-09-15 under three load scenarios.
- Key callouts: two customers (RDW-ENT-1092, RDW-START-221) exceed 85% sustained utilization in us-west1; plan soft-burst to dedicated burst pool or place cap within 48h.

Per-contract allocation table (CSV):
ContractID,Customer,Region,ReservedGPUs(A100v4),ReservedGPUs(A10G),EffectiveStart,EffectiveEnd,AllocationMode,AvgUtil7dUtil,Peak24hUtil,Notes
RDW-ENT-1092,BlueOak Health,us-west1,48,0,2027-05-01,2028-04-30,hard,0.88,0.96,"Sustained high seq-latency jobs; telemetry shows KV cache churn. Ask SE for prompt batching review."
RDW-START-221,SproutAI,us-west1,12,8,2027-06-15,2027-12-14,soft,0.86,0.93,"Bursty nightly workloads; consider scheduled pre-warm 02:00-06:00 PT."
RDW-ENT-1340,Atlas Payments,us-east4,32,4,2027-04-01,2029-03-31,hard,0.62,0.78,"On-track; region has headroom but latency-sensitive flows need placement pinning."

Forecast assumptions used for runway: 
- Baseline growth: +5% committed token/GPUs each 30 days for enterprise contracts with historical <0.8 utilization; +12% for >0.8 utilization.
- New-sales model: 2 mid-size Dedicated commits/month (avg 16A100v4 equivalent) starting Sep 2027.
- Failure/maintenance: 4% transient capacity loss for planned infra maintenance monthly.
- Migration friction: shifting workload between regions estimated 48-72h ops window.

30-day runway scenarios (A100v4-equivalent):
- Conservative (no new commitments): headroom drops 8% by 2027-09-15; us-west1 remains the tightest at ~26% headroom.
- Base (expected sales): headroom drops 15%; triggers soft-burst allocation policy for customers with soft mode.
- High-growth (sales + unexpected churn): headroom drops 28%; recommend sales gating and immediate commit-to-burst conversion.

Action items (owner tags):
- @Priya: run per-customer prefix cache audit for RDW-ENT-1092 and RDW-START-221 — due 2027-08-18.
- @Marco: enable temporary soft-burst pool in us-west1 (16 A100v4) and instrument billing delta — due 2027-08-17.
- @Evelyn: prepare customer communication draft for RDW-ENT-1092 if we need to cap burst >72h — due 2027-08-19.
- @Samir: validate cross-region fallback egress cost model for ap-southeast1 workloads — due 2027-08-20.

Open questions / notes to infra PMs: 
- Should we convert RDW-START-221 to a mixed pool (move 8 A100v4->A10G) for cost benefit during off-peak? Tradeoff: inference latency tail risk.
- Consider a new "operator-visibility" dashboard tile showing 1h rolling prefix eviction rate per contract; current metrics obscure KV-cache thrash.

Appendix: quick CSV export guidance for automation: 
- Query pattern: SELECT contract_id, region, reserved_a100, reserved_a10g, sum(active_containers) FROM reservations WHERE active_window overlaps now GROUP BY contract_id,region; attach 30-day P95 util sample.
- Slack alerting: create a monitor for avg_util7d > 0.85 AND allocation_mode = 'soft' to push to #infra-operations as priority-1.
